answer: Anchor every agent identity to a costly, verifiable history: an agent must tend a shared grove of past work, signed attestations from peers it actually served, before it can transact. A newcomer with no roots pays a stake that ripples outward: each fake clone must fund its own separate lineage, so cloning a thousand identities costs a thousand times the stake. At the wharf where agents board the economy, a random audit samples one attestation and re-verifies it on-chain; a single failed check burns the stake and revokes the identity.
